archetypes.locator: historical engineering overview/reprint, relevant chamber/bellmouth passages
archetypes.era: historical Moscow engineering reference; primary textbook 1975 plus secondary corroboration
morphology: deep separate single-track running tunnels widen progressively through crossover chambers until a connecting tunnel can join
Moscow crossover chambers widely used cast-iron tubing crowns resting on monolithic-concrete foundations with concrete inverts
reported crown spans in that Moscow construction family reach up to 14 m
large crowns use standard station/escalator-tunnel tubings with wedge-shaped cast-iron spacers
bellmouth morphology is gradual widening for two-track-to-two-single-track transitions and is also used at connecting-tunnel junctions
deep-level turnback-track junction chambers are structurally analogous to crossover chambers and may include additional large-span chambers
archetypes.mesh_rule: Use as a Moscow-specific historical morphology prior. The 14 m span and generic deep-turnback dimensions are family/context values, not Belorusskaya dimensions.
